Desired inertia Λ_d  tool frame

The virtual body the hand should feel. Translation is the felt mass along each tool axis (kg); rotation is the felt inertia about each axis (kg·m²). A real object has equal translation on all three — making them unequal feels non-physical, which is the point of exploring. Live-only (needs --serve).

Ablations  paper features

The terms from the draft. Damping is core and ON by default (2 / 0.3) — D_v is what keeps the ungated friction relief passive (eq 37); drag it to 0 only to demonstrate why it is needed. α vel σ is also core and ON (0.03) — the other half of §5.1: it tapers the relief near zero velocity (eq 38) so noise can't dither it, which is what lets the damping stay light. The rest are off (0) — tuned values to try: breakaway 0.35, α sing K₀ 25, detent 4. Cartesian damping D_v resists tool-frame velocity — full strength only below the damp knee (rad/s); above it the drag torque saturates, so guiding-speed motion stays free (raise the knee if the arm feels stiff, lower it if slow creep survives); breakaway adds a load-scaled kick to overcome stiction at rest (no F/T needed); α velocity tapers friction comp near standstill (anti-chatter, knee σ); α singularity tapers it near kinematic singularities (onset K₀); detent is the latched restoring spring that holds an un-driven joint (fixes the near-vertical j2 lean-back); intent floor is the hybrid soft gate — guided motion always gets full relief, un-driven motion (creep/coasting) gets only this fraction, leaving the rest of the friction as a brake (1 = pure paper/ungated, 0 = old hard gate, default 0.5). Live-only (needs --serve).

Command
Reflects b601/balance.py defaults and the calibrated friction/margins in config/b601_rs.toml. Live keys mirror these while dragging: b shaping, bf friction. A browser page can't drive the CAN bus — this sets up the run and shows the state.
